html:
SMTO-EXE-0185 — The cells SMTO was asked to use aren't valid

GUID: ad76d095-a535-5501-b2fc-8818cf9c7070
Slug: office-range-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The spreadsheet step named cells that don't fit together correctly, for example a range written the wrong way, data that doesn't match the size of the range, or a table without proper headers. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Give SMTO the sheet name and the cells as Excel writes them, with the top-left cell first, for example "Sheet1, cells B2 to D10". SMTO only accepts a range that starts at the top-left and ends at the bottom-right inside the sheet.
  2. Make sure the data has the same number of rows and columns as the cell range, with every row the same length. SMTO won't guess where extra or missing values should go.
  3. For a formula, give one single cell and start the formula with an equals sign, for example =SUM(A1:A10). SMTO writes a formula into exactly one cell and only recognises it when it starts with "=".
  4. For a table, make sure the first row has a different text heading in every column and the area doesn't overlap another table. Excel tables need unique headings and can't share cells with another table.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the step and the new copy of the workbook shows your data in the cells you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the sheet and cells you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Excel argument validation rejected a malformed, reversed or out-of-sheet A1 range, a values grid that is ragged or does not match the range size, a multi-cell formula or anchor target, a formula not starting with '=', or invalid table headers, names or overlaps.

What this means

  • Spreadsheet argument validation rejected malformed/reversed/out-of-sheet A1 coordinates, nonrectangular values, dimension mismatch or a formula that lacks the required single-cell/formula syntax. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Spreadsheet argument validation rejected malformed/reversed/out-of-sheet A1 coordinates, nonrectangular values, dimension mismatch or a formula that lacks the required single-cell/formula syntax.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare sheet, A1 bounds, value matrix dimensions and the operation's single-cell or formula requirement.

How to fix it

  • Pass an existing sheet and an A1 range such as B2:D10 with start before end, within XFD1048576; make values a rectangular grid whose rows and columns match the range; use a single cell and a value starting with '=' for excel_set_formula and a single cell for chart anchors; tables need unique non-empty text headers, a valid name, and must not overlap another table.
  • Use an exact sheet plus a finite A1 cell/range and rectangular values matching its dimensions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an exact sheet plus a finite A1 cell/range and rectangular values matching its dimensions.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended range and values agree and pass finite spreadsheet bounds.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
